This means that only incidents that are known to be severe or require immediate attention are shared, which can lead to more targeted and effective interventions.

Studies suggest that sharing data in this way can have several benefits. For instance, research indicates that it can prevent community violence by providing anticipatory patrols and problem-oriented policing strategies. Additionally, improved efficiency of resource deployment is also a possible outcome.

However, the effectiveness of such an approach depends on various factors, including the quality and accuracy of the data collected, as well as the implementation and use of the hotspots method in practice. Nonetheless, the retrieved matches suggest that routinely collecting ambulance data about assaults can be an effective strategy for reducing community violence.
